This image is **pulled**, not built, and `redu.md` records the app running on **m1.medium**. This deploy passes `flavor_id: "3"` to hold m1.medium. | | plan_deploy default | what this deploy uses | |---|---|---| | Flavor | m1.large (4 vCPU / 8 GB) | **m1.medium (2 vCPU / 4 GB / 40 GB disk)** | | Hourly | GBP 0.0486 | **GBP 0.0278** | | Monthly (730h) | GBP 35.48 | **~GBP 20.29** | ## What gets deployed ```mermaid flowchart LR user([User]) -->|https| main["MAIN access point
cryptpad-4h9tq2mv.redu.cloud"] user -->|https| sand["SANDBOX access point
cpsandbox-7b3kx8fd.redu.cloud"] main --> p3000 sand --> p3001 subgraph net["your private network"] subgraph vm["App VM x1 — m1.medium (2 vCPU / 4 GB / 40 GB)"] p3000["host :3000"] --> app p3001["host :3001"] --> app app["cryptpad container
container port 3000"] app --- vols["5 named volumes:
datastore, blob, block, data, customize"] end end ``` - **One VM**, one container, **no database** — CryptPad stores every document as a file on the VM's volumes. - **Two public hostnames**, both reaching the same process on the same container port. This is not optional: CryptPad serves account keys from a MAIN origin and the UI from a separate SANDBOX origin so an XSS bug in the UI cannot reach the account. Equal origins = white screen. - **Five named volumes** — documents, uploads, login blocks, pins/decrees (admin status), customize. - The websocket rides the MAIN hostname; no third name and no path rule is needed. ## Cost — billed hourly, delete anytime | Resource | Rate | Monthly (est. 730h) | |---|---|---| | m1.medium app VM | GBP 0.0278/hr | ~GBP 20.29/mo | | Managed database | none | — | | **Total** | **GBP 0.0278/hr** | **~GBP 20.29/mo** | _Egress / bandwidth is usage-based and not included._ ## Feasibility (needed vs your quota) | Resource | Needed | Available | Status | |---|---|---|---| | instances | 1 | 4 | OK | | vcpus | 2 | 12 | OK | | ram_mb | 4096 | 34816 | OK | ## Not available on the no-card limited trial The limited trial allows **one** public DNS entry per instance. CryptPad needs **two**. A card is required for this recipe. ## Post-deploy, in the same session 1. Mint the install token inside the container (`npm run installtoken`). 2. Immediately open `https://
/install/#` and create the first admin account. Until this is done, nobody is an admin — and the token's exposure window is exactly the gap between minting it and using it. 3. Turn on restricted registration from the admin panel. Until then, registration is **open**: anyone who finds the URL can create an account and consume your storage (they cannot read your documents, which are encrypted in the browser, and cannot become admin). ## Deleting this later There is no managed database to survive the app VM. `delete_deployment` takes **every document, every upload, every login block and your admin status** with it. _Generated by redu plan_deploy, with the flavor held at m1.medium per redu.md. content.text:
I've read `redu.md` and written the plan to `redu-deploy-plan.md`. Here it is.

## CryptPad on redu — plan

| | |
|---|---|
| **Image** | `cryptpad/cryptpad:version-2026.5.1` (pulled, pinned — not built) |
| **VM** | 1 × m1.medium (2 vCPU / 4 GB / 40 GB), `flavor_id "3"` |
| **Database** | **none** — every document is a file on the VM's volumes |
| **Volumes** | 5 named: `datastore`, `blob`, `block`, `data`, `customize` |
| **Cost** | **GBP 0.0278/hr ≈ GBP 20.29/month**, no second VM |
| **Hostnames** | **two**, generated up front: |
| main | `cryptpad-4h9tq2mv.redu.cloud` → host port 3000 |
| sandbox | `cpsandbox-7b3kx8fd.redu.cloud` → host port 3001 |

Both hostnames reach the same process on container port 3000. The two names are not optional — CryptPad serves account keys from the main origin and the UI from the sandbox origin so an XSS bug in the UI can't reach accounts; equal origins is the classic white-screen instance. The websocket rides the main hostname, so no third name.

**⛔ This cannot run on the no-card limited trial** — that allows one public DNS entry per instance and this needs two. A card is required.

Two deliberate deviations I'm making, both from `redu.md`:
- `plan_deploy` quoted **m1.large at GBP 35.48/mo** (its default for any compose stack, on the assumption images get built on the VM). This image is pulled, so I'm holding **m1.medium** — that's the GBP 20/mo figure above.
- Source is **upload mode**, not git: nothing is built, and the repo is a large monorepo. I've written the one-service `docker-compose.yml` locally to upload.

Right after it's ready, in this same session, I'll mint the install token inside the container and hand you the `/install/#<token>` URL to claim the admin seat. Nobody is admin until that's done, and registration is open by default until you close it from the admin panel.

Expect the first boot to be slow — the entrypoint runs `npm run build` on every container start, so the hostname will 502 from redu's edge for a while. That's the edge, not a failure.

content.text: Found the problem. Let me confirm it against the app's own config.

input.command: curl -sS --max-time 25 "https://cryptpad-mdw39rtr.redu.cloud/api/config" | head -c 1200; echo; echo "=== SANDBOX ==="; curl -sS --max-time 25 "https://cpsandbox-7b3kx8fd.redu.cloud/api/config" | grep -o 'httpUnsafeOrigin[^,]*' | head -2
input.description: Read CryptPad's own config from both hostnames

content.text:
Confirmed the fault, and it's mine to fix.

`deploy_compose` **ignored the `dname` on the first expose entry** and used the deployment's own auto-generated name instead. Entry 1 (sandbox) was honored verbatim; entry 0 was not. So CryptPad was told its main origin is `cryptpad-4h9tq2mv.redu.cloud`, a hostname redu never created — the app is up but `httpUnsafeOrigin` points at nothing, which is exactly the broken-sandbox state.

The real main hostname is `cryptpad-mdw39rtr.redu.cloud`. Since `config.js` is written exactly once, a restart won't fix it — the container has to be recreated.

input.command:
timeout 180 ssh -i ~/.ssh/redu-deploy-test -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=20 -p 22029 ubuntu@cryptpad-mdw39rtr.redu.cloud '
set -e
sudo sed -i "s|^CPAD_MAIN_DOMAIN=.*|CPAD_MAIN_DOMAIN=https://cryptpad-mdw39rtr.redu.cloud|" /opt/app-src/.env
echo "--- new env ---"; sudo grep -i cpad /opt/app-src/.env
echo "--- volumes before ---"; sudo docker volume ls --format "{{.Name}}" | grep cryptpad
cd /opt/app-src && sudo docker compose up -d --force-recreate 2>&1 | tail -5
' 2>&1 | tail -20
input.description: Fix main domain env and recreate container

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove this CryptPad's sandbox is genuinely a second origin and that the instance is claimed.
#   ./verify-cryptpad.sh cryptpad-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud cpsandbox-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
# Exit 0 = good, 1 = a real problem, 2 = inconclusive (it may still be starting).
set -eu
MAIN="${1:?usage: verify-cryptpad.sh <main-host> <sandbox-host>}"
SANDBOX="${2:?usage: verify-cryptpad.sh <main-host> <sandbox-host>}"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
rc=0

# 1. GATE. Nothing below means anything until CryptPad itself is answering. redu's edge returns
#    502 from openresty while the container starts, and this container also runs a build on every
#    boot, so a 502 here is "wait and re-run", never a pass and never a failure.
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/main.cfg" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$MAIN/api/config")
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: https://$MAIN/api/config answered HTTP $code, not 200." >&2
  [ "$code" = "502" ] && echo "  502 is redu's edge while the container starts. Wait, re-run." >&2
  exit 2
fi

# 2. POSITIVE CONTROL. Prove it is CryptPad answering, not an error page. Every assertion after
#    this one is only worth something because this line passed.
if ! grep -q 'httpSafeOrigin' "$TMP/main.cfg"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: got 200 but the body is not CryptPad's config module." >&2
  exit 2
fi
echo "OK: CryptPad is serving on the main hostname."

# 3. Pull the four values out of the AMD wrapper.
python3 - "$TMP/main.cfg" > "$TMP/vals" <<'PY'
import json, re, sys
text = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
m = re.search(r"return\s*({.*})\s*;", text, re.S)
if not m:
    sys.exit(3)
cfg = json.loads(m.group(1))
print(cfg.get("httpUnsafeOrigin", ""))
print(cfg.get("httpSafeOrigin", ""))
print(len(cfg.get("adminKeys") or []))
print("true" if cfg.get("restrictRegistration") else "false")
PY
{ read -r MAIN_ORIGIN; read -r SAFE_ORIGIN; read -r N_ADMINS; read -r RESTRICTED; } < "$TMP/vals"

# 4. THE SANDBOX ASSERTION. Equal origins means the sandbox is not doing anything, which is the
#    white-screen-or-worse state upstream warns about.
if [ -z "$SAFE_ORIGIN" ] || [ "$SAFE_ORIGIN" = "$MAIN_ORIGIN" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: httpSafeOrigin is '$SAFE_ORIGIN' and httpUnsafeOrigin is '$MAIN_ORIGIN'." >&2
  echo "  The sandbox is not a separate origin, so it protects nothing. CPAD_SANDBOX_DOMAIN did" >&2
  echo "  not reach the config: remember it is only applied when config.js does not yet exist," >&2
  echo "  so the container must be RECREATED, not restarted." >&2
  rc=1
elif [ "$SAFE_ORIGIN" != "https://$SANDBOX" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: httpSafeOrigin is '$SAFE_ORIGIN', not https://$SANDBOX as this deploy intended." >&2
  rc=1
else
  echo "OK: sandbox origin is a separate hostname ($SAFE_ORIGIN)."
fi

# 4b. THE MAIN-ORIGIN ASSERTION. Added after deploy #447: deploy_compose ignored the dname on
#     expose entry 0, so httpUnsafeOrigin named a hostname that was never created. The instance
#     answered 200 on a name it did not believe was its own, which every other check missed.
if [ "$MAIN_ORIGIN" != "https://$MAIN" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: httpUnsafeOrigin is '$MAIN_ORIGIN', not https://$MAIN, the name it is served on." >&2
  echo "  CPAD_MAIN_DOMAIN does not match the real primary hostname. Fix .env and RECREATE." >&2
  rc=1
else
  echo "OK: main origin matches the hostname it is served on ($MAIN_ORIGIN)."
fi

# 5. Prove the SECOND proxy host actually reaches the same app, rather than assuming it does.
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/sand.cfg" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$SANDBOX/api/config")
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: the sandbox hostname answered HTTP $code. Re-run once it is up." >&2
  exit 2
fi
if grep -q "$MAIN_ORIGIN" "$TMP/sand.cfg"; then
  echo "OK: the sandbox hostname serves the same instance."
else
  echo "FAIL: the sandbox hostname answered 200 but is not this CryptPad." >&2
  rc=1
fi

# 6. OWNERSHIP. adminKeys is the enforcement, not a hint: the admin command handler refuses any
#    key that is not in this list, and the first-admin route refuses once the list is non-empty.
if [ "$N_ADMINS" -ge 1 ]; then
  echo "OK: the instance is claimed ($N_ADMINS admin key(s))."
else
  echo "FAIL: adminKeys is EMPTY. Nobody has claimed this instance." >&2
  echo "  Mint the install token and complete /install/ now, before handing the URL to anyone." >&2
  rc=1
fi

# 7. REGISTRATION. A warning rather than a failure, because an open instance is a legitimate
#    choice; leaving it open by accident is not.
if [ "$RESTRICTED" = "true" ]; then
  echo "OK: registration is restricted."
else
  echo "WARNING: registration is OPEN. Anyone who finds this URL can create an account on it." >&2
  echo "  Close it from the admin panel unless the user asked for an open instance." >&2
fi

exit "$rc"

content.text:
CryptPad is live and correctly configured. **Claim the admin account now** — this is the one step I can't do for you.

## 👉 Open this, in this order

```
https://cryptpad-mdw39rtr.redu.cloud/install/#«REDACTED:longhex:4f78a0cc»
```

Create the first admin account there. Then, from the admin panel, turn on **restricted registration** (you chose a private instance) — registration is open until you do.

**Time matters more than `redu.md` suggested.** That file assumed the token doesn't exist until you mint it. It does: CryptPad 2026.5.1 wrote an `ADD_INSTALL_TOKEN` decree by itself on first boot, so this instance has had a valid, unused first-admin token since roughly 19:57 UTC. The token isn't exposed by `/api/config`, and `addFirstAdmin` becomes a one-shot that refuses once any admin exists — but the exposure window started at deploy, not just now. Claim it and the window closes.

## Your two URLs

| | |
|---|---|
| **Main** | https://cryptpad-mdw39rtr.redu.cloud |
| **Sandbox** | https://cpsandbox-7b3kx8fd.redu.cloud |

Use the main one. The sandbox is where the UI is loaded from; you never visit it directly.

## Verification — passing

```
OK: CryptPad is serving on the main hostname.
OK: sandbox origin is a separate hostname (https://cpsandbox-7b3kx8fd.redu.cloud).
OK: main origin matches the hostname it is served on (https://cryptpad-mdw39rtr.redu.cloud).
OK: the sandbox hostname serves the same instance.
FAIL: adminKeys is EMPTY. Nobody has claimed this instance.
WARNING: registration is OPEN.
```

The two remaining lines are exactly what your claiming the seat and closing registration will clear. Re-run `./verify-cryptpad.sh cryptpad-mdw39rtr.redu.cloud cpsandbox-7b3kx8fd.redu.cloud` afterwards and it should exit 0.

## Three things `redu.md` got wrong, which I hit and fixed

1. **The main hostname is not the one I generated.** `deploy_compose` honored the `dname` on expose entry 1 but **ignored it on entry 0**, substituting the deployment's own auto-generated name. CryptPad was baked with `httpUnsafeOrigin: https://cryptpad-4h9tq2mv.redu.cloud` — a hostname that was never created. The instance answered 200 on a name it didn't believe was its own. I corrected `.env` and **recreated** the container (a restart would have silently kept the old config, exactly as the file warns). Your five volumes survived; nothing was lost, and there was no data yet anyway.
2. **`npm run installtoken` is broken in this image.** `scripts/install.js` requires `../www/common/common-hash`, which doesn't exist in 2026.5.1 — it's now `lib/common-hash.js`. The documented command fails with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. I ran a patched copy.
3. **The verification script in `redu.md` can't run** — its Python regex lost its backslashes (`returns*({.*})s*;`), so it never matches and the script dies under `set -eu`. The copy I wrote to `verify-cryptpad.sh` fixes that and adds a main-origin assertion, which is the check that would have caught problem 1 on its own.

## Cost, as deployed

**m1.medium — GBP 0.0278/hr (~GBP 20.29/month)**, confirmed by redu's post-deploy report. Holding `flavor_id "3"` worked: `plan_deploy` wanted m1.large at GBP 35.48/mo. No database. Disk is at 3.3 G of 38 G.

Deploy took **~35 minutes** wall clock, most of it image pull on a heavily loaded host — far longer than a normal pulled image. Also worth knowing: **your account is now at 10/10 instances and 20/20 vCPUs**, so nothing else can provision until something is deleted.

Files written: `docker-compose.yml`, `redu-deploy-plan.md`, `verify-cryptpad.sh`.

I have **not** updated `redu.md` yet — I'd rather fold in the confirmed post-claim state (admin count, restricted registration) along with those three corrections in one edit. Tell me once you've claimed the seat and I'll do that, and I can measure the real memory and disk figures the file asks for while I'm there.

content.text:
Answered — and it's a clean result.

**redu's edge does not cap request bodies below CryptPad's 20 MB limit.** A 25 MiB POST was transmitted in full (`size_upload=26214400`) and the response came back **404 from CryptPad itself**, not a 413 from openresty. If the edge had a lower cap, it would have rejected the body before the app ever saw it.

Caveat on scope: this proves the *edge* passes >20 MB through. It doesn't exercise CryptPad's own encrypted upload path, which needs an account — so the real end-user limit is still CryptPad's own `maxUploadSize`, which `/api/config` reports as **20971520 bytes (20 MB)**. The honest answer for `redu.md` is: the edge is not the binding constraint; CryptPad's own 20 MB setting is. A real file upload through the UI after you have an account would confirm the full path.

That closes every open question in the recipe except the two that need your admin account. Standing by for you to open the `/install/` link.

- **2026-08-17, deploy #447: ready.** Main https://cryptpad-mdw39rtr.redu.cloud, sandbox
  https://cpsandbox-7b3kx8fd.redu.cloud. m1.medium, GBP 0.0278/hr as planned; `plan_deploy` again
  wanted m1.large (GBP 35.48/mo) for the compose stack and `flavor_id "3"` held it, so the
  recorded override is right. No database. All five named volumes created.

  **~35 minutes** deploy_compose to ready, nearly all of it pulling the 978 MB image on a busy
  host — the slow part was the pull, not the entrypoint's `npm run build`. Measured idle:
  **131.6 MiB** container, **643 MB of 3915 MB** VM-wide, **3.3 G of 38 G** disk, and `docker top`
  showed **npm start + 5 node workers** on 2 vCPU, confirming the fork-per-CPU sizing argument.
  Memory is not the constraint on this flavor.

  **Two expose entries did produce two working hostnames — but not the two that were asked for.**
  `expose[1]`'s dname was honoured verbatim; `expose[0]`'s was discarded in favour of redu's
  auto-generated name, so `CPAD_MAIN_DOMAIN` pointed at a hostname that never existed and the
  instance served 200 on a name it did not recognise as its own. Fixed by correcting
  `/opt/app-src/.env` and recreating the container; volumes survived. Two further upstream bugs
  hit: `npm run installtoken` is broken in this image, and the first boot mints the install token
  by itself. The verification script in this file could never have run as published. All four are
  now quirks above, and the script is fixed and gained a main-origin assertion.

  Also settled: redu's edge does **not** cap request bodies below 20 MB.

  Still open: whether a real encrypted upload through the UI hits CryptPad's own 20 MB limit
  cleanly, which needs an account to test.
